Question B-003-018-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Touching the person before the source is de-energized can make the rescuer part of the circuit.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "De-energize the power source before touching the person": This is the correct choice because touching the person before the source is de-energized can make the rescuer part of the circuit.
- sourceIndex 1: "Wrap the person in a blanket and pull him to a safe area": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from De-energize the power source before touching the person. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Call an electrician": This answer would fit a different fault than De-energize the power source before touching the person. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Remove the person by pulling an arm or a leg": This option confuses another station topic with De-energize the power source before touching the person. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
